findings.evidence: grep '^def gh' scripts: toolchain_tags.py:160 `def gh(path, jq=None):`, resolve_deps.py:98 `def gh(path, jq=None, paginate=False):`, pr_status/core.py:119 `def gh_api(path, jq=None, paginate=False):`
findings.fix: Import `pr_status.core.gh_api` (toolchain_tags.py:72-74 already does `sys.path.insert(..., "pr_status")` to import zulip, so the precedent and the path hack exist), or hoist the one wrapper into a shared module and have toolchain_tags.gh/gh_optional use it. Delete the local copy either way.
findings.issue: `gh(path, jq=None, paginate=False)` is a third copy of the `gh api` subprocess wrapper. `scripts/toolchain_tags.py:160` has the identical body (`cmd = ["gh", "api", path] + (["--jq", jq] if jq else [])`, same RuntimeError text), and `scripts/pr_status/core.py:119` has the same signature `gh_api(path, jq=None, paginate=False)` plus rate-limit retry. The resolver issues dozens of calls per run (the 2026-10-03 fixture records ~60 distinct answers) with no rate-limit handling, so it will hard-fail where core.gh_api would wait.

findings.evidence: check-bump.sh:163-167 vs resolve_deps.py:166-173; both select completed+successful build.yml runs on head_sha with head_branch == master.
findings.fix: Put the predicate in one place (e.g. a `mathlib_cache_published(gh, repo, sha, tag)` in a shared module) and have check-bump.sh call it the same way it now calls `parse_toolchain` (check-bump.sh:187-197 shells into `lean_versions` via `sys.path.insert`), instead of keeping the jq filter in bash.
findings.issue: `GitHub.cache_published` re-implements the cache signal check-bump.sh step 2b already performs (check-bump.sh:163-167: `workflows/build.yml/runs?head_sha=...&event=push`, filtered on `head_branch == "master" and status == "completed" and conclusion == "success"`). The resolver's docstring (lines 30-33) and docs/dependency-bumps.md line 34 state the two must ask the same question, and the status table plans to extend the guard with the `release_cache.yml` signal the resolver already encodes - so the copy is slated to grow. This is the same drift risk that motivated factoring parse_toolchain into lean_versions; if the two predicates diverge, the resolver proposes pins the guard rejects.

findings.evidence: grep parse_release scripts/: only toolchain_tags.py:77 (import line) and lean_versions.py definitions; test_toolchain_tags.py:27,28,32 call `tt.parse_release`. The other re-exported names are genuinely used (release_key:267, release_of_toolchain:140, release_refs:217, tag_commit:222, TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX:364).
findings.fix: Drop `parse_release` from the import list, move the `VersionNames` test class into a new `scripts/test_lean_versions.py` importing `lean_versions` directly, and add it to ci.yml next to `test_resolve_deps.py`.
findings.issue: `parse_release` is imported (under `# noqa: F401`) but never called anywhere in toolchain_tags.py after the move; its only consumers are `test_toolchain_tags.py:27-32` (`tt.parse_release`). That is a re-export kept to preserve the pre-move surface, which the compatibility policy forbids, and test_resolve_deps.py:238 points at it ("parsing and ordering are lean_versions', tested through test_toolchain_tags.py").

findings.evidence: lean_versions.py:70-72 vs toolchain_tags.py:220-223 - identical comprehension over `release_refs` + `tag_commit`.
findings.fix: Give `release_tags(gh, repo, resolve=None)` an optional resolver (`resolve = resolve or gh`) and make existing_tags `return lean_versions.release_tags(gh_optional, REPO, resolve=gh)`.
findings.issue: `existing_tags()` restates the body of the new `lean_versions.release_tags` (lean_versions.py:71): both are `{name: tag_commit(gh, repo, sha, kind) for name, (sha, kind) in release_refs(gh, repo).items()}`, differing only in using gh_optional for the listing. Same problem class as the above: the PR added the shared combinator and left a copy behind.

summary: The lean_versions extraction is real de-duplication, but the new resolver re-implements three helpers the repo already has: the `gh api` wrapper, the mathlib cache-published predicate (duplicated against check-bump.sh in bash), and a leftover re-export of a function moved into lean_versions. Fix by reusing the located helpers; everything else in the PR is genuinely new.
